firing: os._exit(86) — an exception could be caught and turned into a success
sandbox_rule: the path being written must resolve inside TRADING_BOT_FAILPOINT_SANDBOX, otherwise FailpointRefused

points.name: ledger.before_write
points.durable_before: every previous ledger row; no part of this one
points.post_crash: the row does not exist; the book is untouched by this bar

points.name: ledger.after_write
points.durable_before: the bytes are in the OS page cache, not fsynced
points.post_crash: under a process crash the row is usually visible; under power loss it may not be. The two are not distinguishable here — declared in the report

points.name: ledger.after_fsync
points.durable_before: the row is durable; the book still lacks its effect
points.post_crash: projection ahead of authority: the resume re-executes the bar and the identity suppresses the duplicate row

points.name: book.before_save
points.durable_before: the previous book (seed) and the ledger rows of this bar
points.post_crash: seed book; the effect is not committed

points.name: book.after_tmp_write
points.durable_before: a partly written BOOK.json.tmp; BOOK.json still the seed
points.post_crash: temporary file unusable and never adopted

points.name: book.after_tmp_fsync
points.durable_before: a complete, fsynced BOOK.json.tmp; BOOK.json still the seed
points.post_crash: orphan tmp; recover() reports it, load() ignores it

points.name: book.after_prev_copy
points.durable_before: BOOK.json.prev == the seed; BOOK.json still the seed
points.post_crash: seed book; the rotation is harmless because the current generation never moved

points.name: book.after_replace
points.durable_before: BOOK.json is the new book (COMMIT); no COMMIT event, no directory fsync
points.post_crash: committed intermediate book; recover() reports commit_event_lag and accepts it

points.name: book.after_dir_fsync
points.durable_before: as after_replace; on nt the directory fsync is a no-op, so this point is the same window

points.name: event.after_write
points.durable_before: a COMMIT row in the OS cache; the book already committed
points.post_crash: the resume sees the book and a torn tail it classifies, never a rolled-back book

points.name: event.after_fsync
points.post_crash: a committed bar whose ACK exists; two resumes must change nothing

points.name: bar.before_commit
points.durable_before: the bar's economic ledger rows; the book still at the previous barrier
points.post_crash: no effect committed; the resume re-executes the bar

points.name: bar.after_commit
points.durable_before: the book and its COMMIT event are both durable (ACK reached)
points.post_crash: committed bar; the resume starts after its barrier

points.name: lock.after_acquire
points.durable_before: the lock file is on disk (takeover path at 367, first acquisition at 373)
points.post_crash: an orphan lock whose pid is gone: the next process takes it over

not_instrumented_on_purpose.why: it is the same window as book.after_prev_copy: the current generation has not moved, so the crash leaves the seed book
the primitive is atomic or fails; a failpoint inside the syscall would be a kernel fault injection, not a runtime one
